title: Homology concentration conjecture for matching complexes
statement:
Let $d>1$ be a positive integer and let $A$ be a finite set. The matching complex $C_A^d$ is the simplicial complex whose vertices are the $d$-element subsets of $A$ and whose faces consist of mutually disjoint such subsets. For $n=1,\ldots,3d-1$, consider the matching complex $C_{nd}^d$ on a set of cardinality $nd$, and write $\widetilde H_i$ for its reduced homology groups.

**Matching-complex homology conjecture.** The only non-zero homology group of $C_{nd}^d$ for $n=1,\ldots,3d-1$ is

$$
\widetilde H_{n-2}(C_{nd}^d).
$$

Via the correspondence between syzygies of Veronese embeddings and homology of matching complexes, this is presented as equivalent to the Ottaviani–Paoletti conjecture. Since the latter is proved for third Veronese embeddings in the source, this equivalent formulation is solved in the case $d=3$; the general statement is not resolved by the supplied text.
source_name: Thanh Vu, “N_6 property for third Veronese embeddings”, arXiv:1303.5532 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.5532

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)
